prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity 1600 by 1000 landscape desktop application mockup for WARCODE, a personal AI coding agent. This is a working coding application screen, edge-to-edge, no laptop or photographic frame.
Structure in exact order: a shallow native titlebar showing Warcode, a 230px project/session navigation rail, a broad 850px conversation and composer work area, a 420px file-change review panel. A thin bottom status bar. Preserve recognizable coding workflows: projects, sessions, conversation, model selection, files, changes, settings. The content is an illustrative coding session, no commercial claims.
Visual identity: flight director workstation translated into calm contemporary software. Matte graphite #101418, elevated panels #1B2229, readable soft-white #E9EDF0, warm amber #F4B544 reserved for active navigation and primary actions, subtle cool slate separators. Sharp professional typographic hierarchy, Barlow Semi Condensed for the compact WARCODE wordmark and display titles, Barlow or Inter for readable 13–15px interface text, IBM Plex Mono only for code. Angular abstract W icon composed of three clear strokes, paired with wordmark WARCODE. Crisp flat surfaces, moderate 6px radii, precise alignment, no gradients, no glow, no military clip art, no decorative gauges.
Content: sidebar brand WARCODE; New session action; project CodingHarness; sessions “Refine the workspace”, “Fix auth callback”, “Add keyboard shortcuts”; bottom Settings. Top main header “Refine the workspace” with branch “warcode-rebrand”. Conversation with user request “Simplify the project sidebar and improve keyboard navigation.” Assistant reply “I’ll update the sidebar structure, then check focus and keyboard navigation.” A concise tool activity row “Edited sidebar.tsx”. Show a readable small code change card, then response “The sidebar now groups sessions by project. Keyboard focus follows the visible order.” Composer with text “Ask Warcode to build something…” and controls “Build”, “Claude Sonnet”, an amber send button. Right review heading “Changes”, file sidebar.tsx selected, a genuinely readable sample TypeScript diff with muted green additions, tabs Files and Review. Bottom says “Local workspace” and “All changes saved”. Keep all visible spelling exact. Demonstrate dense and quiet regions with excellent contrast. Restrained and usable enough for long daily coding sessions. No OpenCode text or original OpenCode O logo.
